commit(address,uint256,uint256).details: The caller must approve this router for assets. Exactly assets is pulled in total:      the rounded-down fee goes straight to feeRecipient, and the net goes through this      router into the vault. Zero fees skip the fee transfer. Shares go directly to the caller.      The vault allowance is limited to net and reset to zero after deposit; pre-existing      USDC is preserved and cannot be spent. Nonzero assets always leave at least one base      unit for the deposit because feeBps is at most 100. All checks possible before external      interactions are performed first; nonReentrant protects the transfer/deposit sequence.      The caller must receive nonzero shares and at least the number reported by the vault.      Slippage is checked against the actual increase in the caller's share balance.      Share-delivery, slippage, or balance-preservation failures revert the entire transaction,      including fee payment. No fee is charged when withdrawing directly from the vault.      Arithmetic overflow reverts for unrepresentably large fee products.

params.assets: Total USDC base units to commit, including the fee.
params.minShares: Minimum acceptable delivered shares; zero still requires nonzero delivery.
params.vault: Permanently allowlisted ERC-4626 vault to receive the net deposit.

@title CommitRouter
 @notice Non-custodial USDC deposit router for permanently allowlisted ERC-4626 vaults,
         including compatible Morpho Vault V2 vaults on Arc.
 @dev The fixed basis-point fee is charged only on commit, never on withdrawal.
      Users own their shares immediately and withdraw directly from the vault; the router
      never holds shares. USDC is held only transiently during a successful commit.
      Approving the router lets it pull exactly the amount the user commits, split between
      the fee recipient and the vault deposit; no third party can commit another user's funds.
      There is no admin, owner, setter, upgrade path, payable function, or rescue function.
      Stray tokens sent to the router are not recoverable and do not block commits.
      Every successful commit preserves the router's pre-existing USDC balance.
      WARNING: If the USDC issuer blocklists feeRecipient, every fee-bearing commit reverts
      for as long as the blocklist persists, potentially forever, because the recipient is
      immutable. Commits whose fee rounds down to zero skip that transfer and are an exception.
      Allowlisting checks the vault's asset only at construction; it does not guarantee vault
      safety, availability, share value, or immutable vault implementation and configuration.
